title: CLAUDE.md's Delegation block still says documenter ships without Bash; OFLE-44 fixed that upstream on 2026-09-13
description:
Found while working LCLI-640 (2026-09-29), when the profile work put me in a position to read the documenter agent's tool list. Not in LCLI-640's scope; filed rather than absorbed.

CLAUDEMD line 53-55 (the second bullet of the Delegation block's 'two things that are not optional, both learned the hard way on 2026-09-13') reads: 'Read the agent's tool list before dispatching. documenter ships with no Bash, so it cannot run lore, lore check, or git -- every documentation deliverable in this repo needs all three. Route doc work to implementer until that is fixed upstream.'

The claim was TRUE when written and the condition it waits on has since been met, so the instruction is now stale and actively misroutes work away from the correct specialist.

EVIDENCE, read by ref from opum-fleet's own repository rather than from an installed copy. At a0bec17 (2026-09-09, the plugin's first commit) agents/documenter.md carried 'tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Skill' -- no Bash, so the bullet was accurate when lore-cli wrote it in 80099c94 on 2026-09-13. f717ba8 (2026-09-13, 'fix(OFLE-44): give the documenter subagent Bash so it can run the lore workflow it's instructed to', opum-ai/opum-fleet#83) added Bash, the same day. At opum-fleet origin/dev the line is now 'tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash, Skill'.

Corroborated on the installed side too, and the cache agrees: every opum-workflow version present on this machine from 0.7.2 (installed 2026-09-15) through 0.10.11 grants documenter Bash, and 0.10.11 is the in-use version (seven active PID markers in its .in_use directory). The oldest installed version postdates the claim, so the by-ref history above, not the cache, is what dates it.

The bullet's PRINCIPLE -- read the agent's tool list before dispatching -- is what caught this and should stay. Only its conclusion about documenter is obsolete.

NOTE, so the fix is not over-read: this correction does not by itself make documenter the right dispatch for every doc task here. What it removes is a stated reason that was never true after 2026-09-13.

acceptanceCriteria.text: CLAUDE.md no longer tells a session to route documentation work to implementer on the grounds that documenter lacks Bash; the tool-list principle is kept, the fact is corrected, and the met condition is recorded with the commit that met it
The corrected text is verified against opum-fleet agents/documenter.md BY REF at both the fix commit and origin/dev, not against an installed plugin copy
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0 (CLAUDE.md is read by three required CI jobs per this repository profile block)

implementationNotes: OWNERSHIP RECORDED (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-29, on the LCLI-640 renewal boundary): "LCLI-643 is a CLAUDE.md edit in your repository, so it is yours to decide or take to your own user. I'm only noting it exists." So there is no cross-repository blocker and no approval to wait on from the fleet: the file is this repository's own governing document, and the session that owns it decides. Recorded because the alternative reading -- that a peer's note about the documenter agent's tool list might need the plugin repository's agreement -- would have parked this task behind a question that does not exist. The evidence in the description stands and was not re-measured here: the claim was true when written, opum-fleet f717ba8 fixed it the same day, and every installed opum-workflow version grants documenter Bash.
